transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Ana (Redwood SE), Lina (BrightEdge CTO), Mark (Infra), Priya (ML)

Summary: weekly POC check-in for throughput optimization - continuous batching, concurrency targets, queueing behavior, and next steps

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, do people have video on?
[00:07] Lina: yep, hi, sorry we ran a little late, had an internal standup overrun
[00:12] Samir: no worries. quick agenda - ana will walk through last week's bench, then we talk config changes and next steps
[00:18] Ana: cool, so last run was the 6 hour baseline we did last thursday, using the Redwood hosted variant with continuous batching turned on, concurrency target set to 12, queue size default. we replayed ~100k requests derived from your sample traffic
[00:34] Mark: quick q — that sample was the truncated sample you asked for? i think we trimmed the long-chat type requests out, yep
[00:40] Ana: right, we removed 5% of the outliers to stabilize the bench but kept the real arrival distribution
[00:46] Ana: results summary: avg tokens/sec per GPU was ~42k, throughput ~220 reqs/sec, latency p50 ~62ms, p95 ~210ms, p99 was spikey up to 1.8s during bursts
[01:03] Priya: 1.8s for p99 sounds high, when did those spikes happen?
[01:08] Ana: mostly when there were small bursts of concurrent requests that exceeded the concurrency target and requests queued; because KV cache warmup was also happening early in the test we saw extra variance
[01:18] Samir: to be clear, queuing happens at the router layer when concurrency cap reached; continuous batching tries to fill batches but if requests arrive too fast they wait for slot which causes tail to increase
[01:30] Lina: our SLO is p95 < 250ms and p99 < 700ms ideally, so that p99 is problematic
[01:40] Mark: also, we have a hard throughput goal of 10k user interactions / hour, which maps to these req/sec numbers, so cost matters too
[01:50] Ana: noted. we ran a second test with concurrency increased to 20, same batching config. throughput improved to ~340 reqs/sec, p95 down to 160ms, p99 ~520ms but still some outliers at ~1.1s
[02:05] Priya: were you using prefix caching / KV cache for repeated contexts?
[02:10] Ana: yes, KV cache enabled for warm prefixes but during ramp the cold-starts and model kv resizing caused a bit of jitter — sometimes the inference runtime mislabels as K-V cash in the logs, ha
[02:22] Samir: (laughs) classic transcription of K-V cash
[02:25] Lina: can we quantify how much of the p99 is due to network vs model execution vs queueing?
[02:31] Ana: we added tags in the trace, rough breakdown: during spikes ~55% queue wait, ~30% model execution, ~15% network/overheads. but that's rounded and the instrumentation has some noise
[02:45] Mark: that suggests increasing concurrency further, or improving batching behavior? tradeoff is cost per GPU if we just raise concurrency limit right?
[02:55] Samir: exactly — increasing concurrency means each GPU serves more simultaneous KS (oops) — more concurrency gives lower tail but may reduce per-token throughput if context switching occurs; also depends on memory for KV cache, sequence length, and quantization profile
[03:10] Priya: what about queueing policies — can we prioritize small interactive requests vs large long-form jobs?
[03:16] Ana: yep, Redwood supports route-level prioritization and queue weights. we can give interactive traffic higher priority and prefer small batch sizes for them. continuous batching can also be tuned with min batch fill and max latency thresholds
[03:30] Samir: another lever is autoscaling/burst capacity for Dedicated — we can provision burst nodes for peak windows to avoid queuing entirely during traffic spikes
[03:40] Lina: we've been trying to avoid large Reserved Dedicated costs; prefer to keep hosted but still need reliable p99s
[03:46] Samir: understood. we sketched three options last week: 1) keep hosted, tune concurrency and prioritization; 2) Dedicated reserved with smaller buffer for bursts; 3) Hybrid route-level routing to cheaper variants for background tasks
[03:58] Mark: curious — did you measure effective batch sizes during the run?
[04:02] Ana: yes, avg batch size was 12 when concurrency 12, and bumped to 16 avg at concurrency 20. we saw a small gain in token throughput but diminishing returns after ~18-20 avg batch because sequence lengths in your workload are short (median 64 tokens)
[04:20] Priya: sequence lengths are short most of the time, yeah. some long chats exist but rare
[04:25] Ana: so recommended next test plan: run 24h steady-state with concurrency ladder: 12 -> 16 -> 20 -> 24, holding each for 3 hours to gather P50/P95/P99 and batch histograms; include a controlled burst window for each stage
[04:40] Samir: and we'll add route prioritization for interactive route, and an alternate small-batch config to compare
[04:47] Lina: sounds good. what about queue size and timeouts? our user flows expect 10s timeout max but we prefer 3s ideally
[04:55] Ana: default queue timeout set to 5s in our bench; we can reduce to 3s to prevent huge waits, but that increases observed error rate if concurrency insufficient; we'll show tradeoffs in the bench results
[05:07] Mark: any network-level knobs? our infra team saw a few NIC interrupts last week during the 4pm spike
[05:11] Samir: we asked you to share NIC telemetry, that will help identify whether packet drops are contributing to tail
[05:20] Mark: noted, will send later today
[05:23] Priya: on model side, did you try a quantized variant for lower perf? we were worried about quality drift
[05:29] Ana: we tested an 8-bit quantized build in the earlier PoC; it improved token throughput by ~15% but increased p99 variance slightly for long sequences. for your short sequences it may be net positive; we should include it as a config in the 24h run
[05:45] Samir: good call. include quantized and full precision variants so you can compare quality vs cost
[05:51] Lina: how will you present results? we need clear per-route dashboards and a CSV with raw samples
[05:57] Ana: we'll provide the dashboard link and a csv export with tagged samples; also include a small write-up of configuration used per stage
[06:06] Samir: ok action items then: ana run the 24h ladder bench and share results, samir send updated pricing, priya/mark share traffic histogram + NIC telemetry
[06:16] Lina: one more question — what about SSO/keys for the dedicated pilot? we need to test SAML flow for infra team
[06:22] Samir: that's separate but we can loop in our security team; for the bench we can use short-lived API keys; we'll schedule a security review next week if you want
[06:31] Mark: please include any compliance docs for on-prem/dedicated options in the next email
[06:36] Samir: will do. quick note — we saw one weird log where the runtime reported an "OOM reserve" which was probably due to batch resizing; ana can look into that trace specifically
[06:45] Ana: i have the trace id, will attach in the results package
[06:49] Priya: thanks, also can we try a concurrency cap policy that scales automatically with request rate? dynamic cap?
[06:55] Ana: we have basic dynamic concurrency heuristics we can enable in the bench — it slowly raises concurrency as CPU/GPU metrics look healthy; we'll include a run with that enabled as an experiment
[07:06] Lina: ok good. anything else on tuning?
[07:10] Samir: just to reiterate — we'll tune three levers: concurrency target, queue timeouts/priorities, and batching thresholds (min fill / max wait). plus optionally quantization and dynamic concurrency
[07:22] Mark: cost modeling question — if we move to concurrency 24 steady-state what sort of cost delta? rough estimate?
[07:28] Ana: depends on utilization. if utilization remains high, cost per token goes down; but if we increase idle capacity, cost rises. rough back-of-envelope: moving from 12->24 concurrency doubled capacity for burst handling, but if steady utilization is half you pay ~30% more in reserved nodes for safety; we'll give a modeled sheet with numbers
[07:47] Priya: please include quality regression checks — we care about hallucinations or subtle output drift with quantized models
[07:53] Ana: will add eval prompts and run automatic regressions on the bench outputs
[07:58] Lina: great. schedule next sync after you share bench results?
[08:02] Samir: yes — we'll circle back once the 24h run completes, target to have findings by friday 2026-07-10 and meet early next week if needed
[08:10] Mark: thanks all
[08:12] Meeting end

Notes on transcript: some words were mis-transcribed (K-V cache -> K-V cash, oom reserve -> OOM-reserve) and speaker names slightly abbreviated in the system export.
